title: Chemical short-range order increases the phonon heat conductivity in a refractory high-entropy alloy

recollection.starting_material: Likely a refractory high-entropy alloy of early transition metals such as Nb–Mo–Ta–W or Hf–Nb–Ti–Zr
recollection.intervention: Inducing chemical short-range order by heat treatment/annealing (contrasted with a rapidly quenched, more randomly disordered state); characterization with scattering techniques and first-principles or MD simulations
recollection.structure: A single-phase bcc solid solution in which partial chemical ordering (short-range correlations between specific element pairs) develops upon annealing
recollection.mechanism: Short-range order reduces mass/fluctuation and force-constant disorder seen by phonons, lengthening their mean free paths and thus enhancing lattice thermal conductivity
recollection.results: Room-temperature phonon (lattice) thermal conductivity roughly doubles compared with the fully random state (e.g. increasing from ~6–8 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹ to ~12–16 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹); modeling reproduces the trend and attributes it to reduced phonon scattering at mid-to-high frequencies

score.note: Correctly identifies induction of chemical short-range order and the broad mechanism of reduced phonon scattering, but incorrectly attributes the intervention to annealing rather than Monte Carlo-controlled SRO. It misses the specific B2-like HfTi/TiZr clusters and percolative pathways. The claimed near-doubling of conductivity is far from the actual ~12% increase.
